title: Monkey Grip
author: Helen Garner
review: A suffocating portrait of love and obsession. The difficulty of pulling away from someone when you know they’re not good for you. Characters all seemed so self-destructive but relatable.

title: On Earth We’re Briefly Gorgeous
author: Ocean Vuong
review: Poetic rhythms. An immigrant story set through the eyes of three generations. Exploration of queerness in the immigrant/American macho body. Also deals with the opioid crisis in a profound way, not bleeding heart but absolutely heartbreaking in the narrators matter-of-fact telling of all the people he has lost to it.

title: Child’s Play
author: David Malouf
review: Definitely not my favourite Malouf. Felt unsettled the whole time by the narrators play around the facts of the event. Intentionally uneasy but for that reason I found it hard to want to go back to read it. Very small but took me almost two weeks.

title: The Dinner
author: Herman Koch
review: Thriller looking at parents and their children. The dad is a psychopath and apparently you can test for that in utero?? Interesting study of social politics in Denmark. I liked the way it began to unravel and slowly reveal the truth, with the narrator never quite spelling anything out but we gain the whole picture and the horrifying consequences.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
review: I just didn’t get it? They were all awful.

title: Into Thin Air
author: Jon Krakauer
review: So informative about the processes that get people up Everest. Heartbreaking even when you know what’s coming. One of the best journalistic non-fiction books I’ve read.

title: Gould’s Book of Fish
author: Richard Flanagan
review: He’s done it again. Another beautifully lyrical and poetic book about Tassie. In turns darkly comic and gut wrenchingly tragic. Magical realism that I like.

title: All That Man Is
author: David Szalay
review: God I love a collection of short stories. All with the through line of men trying to figure themselves out. Reminded me a lot of Jonathan Franzen. Terribly flawed people, just like us.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
review: Much better than I expected. Damn these girls really were just like us and boys get nervous around girls and nothing has changed for hundreds of years. First half was a little slow but the second half really hooked me.

title: Joe Cinque’s Consolation
author: Helen Garner
review: Riveting exploration of the legal system and the human forces behind it. Exploration of morality, and the essence of being human, to love and to lose.

title: Flesh
author: David Szalay
review: Couldn’t put it down. And the gut punch at the end left me feeling winded and morose for days. That a human life can span so much, so many ups and downs.

title: Yesteryear
author: Caro Claire Burke
review: Interesting and twisting and turning. Not really groundbreaking and there were plot holes that I struggled through. Definitely could have been more nuanced. But otherwise very entertaining.
